note_claims.claim: The patient presented with a head injury following a mechanical fall at home at approximately 09:30.
The patient sustained the injury by tripping on a rug and striking the left side of her head on a door frame.
The daughter reports the patient was muddled for approximately 10 minutes after the fall, although the patient has no memory of this.
Loss of consciousness is uncertain and unwitnessed.
The patient experienced one episode of vomiting in the car.
The patient reported a mild headache at the impact site.
The patient has no visual disturbance, limb weakness, or neck pain.
There was no preceding dizziness or presyncope.
The last dose of apixaban was taken this morning, after the fall.
The patient is up to date with tetanus.
The patient is prescribed Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily for heart rhythm.
The patient is prescribed Amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
The patient is allergic to penicillin, which causes swelling.
The Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) is 15.
There is a 3 cm laceration with a haematoma over the right temple.
Pupils are equal and reactive to light.
Strength is normal everywhere (normal power in all limbs).
There is no cervical spine midline tenderness.
The heart rate is irregular at about 80.
The blood pressure is 146/82.
The patient has a head injury in an anticoagulated 81-year-old with brief post-traumatic confusion and amnesia, and one episode of vomiting.
A CT scan of the head is required due to the patient being on a blood thinner.
The evening's dose of apixaban will be withheld until the CT scan is reviewed.
The wound will be cleaned and closed with steri-strips.
If the CT scan is normal, the patient can be discharged with the daughter, who will stay with her for 24 hours.
The patient should call 999 or return immediately if she becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
Written head injury advice was given to the daughter.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician introduced herself as Dr Pemberton to Mrs Castellan.
The relative identified herself as the patient's daughter, Sue.
The clinician asked Mrs Castellan what happened.
The patient stated she tripped on the rug in the hall and banged her head on the door frame.
The clinician asked what time the fall occurred.
The patient initially stated the time was about half past nine.
The relative corrected the time, stating it was about quarter to eight, noting the post hadn't come and the patient hadn't had breakfast.
The patient acknowledged the correction, saying, 'Oh, she's probably right.'
The clinician asked which side the patient hit.
The patient stated she hit the left side, 'by my eye.'
The clinician asked if the patient had blacked out.
The patient stated, 'I don't think so.'
The relative reported that when she arrived ten minutes later, the patient was muddled and kept asking what day it was for about ten minutes.
The clinician asked the patient if she remembered the relative's observation.
The patient stated she did not remember the daughter arriving.
The clinician asked if the patient had been sick.
The relative stated the patient was sick once in the car on the way to the clinic.
The patient denied being sick, stating, 'I don't remember that either.'
The clinician asked if the patient had any headache now.
The patient reported a bit of a headache where she hit it.
The clinician asked about problems with vision or weakness in arms or legs.
The patient stated, 'No.'
The clinician asked about neck pain.
The patient stated, 'No, my neck's fine.'
The clinician asked if the patient felt dizzy or faint before the fall.
The patient stated she did not feel dizzy and explained she caught her foot on the rug.
The clinician asked what medicines the patient was on.
The relative listed the patient's medications: Apixaban 2.5 milligrams twice a day for heart rhythm, Bisoprolol 2.5 milligrams once a day, and Amlodipine 5 mg.
The clinician asked when the patient last took the apixaban.
The patient stated she took the apixaban this morning with her breakfast, after the fall.
The clinician asked about allergies.
The patient stated she is allergic to penicillin, which makes her swell up.

The clinician performed an examination, noting the patient's eyes were open, she was talking normally, GCS was 15, there was a 3 cm cut with a bump around it on the left temple, pupils were equal and reactive, and strength was normal everywhere.
The patient responded, 'Okay.'
The clinician pressed on the back of the patient's neck and asked about pain.
The patient stated, 'No.'
The clinician noted the patient's heart rate was irregular at about 80 and the blood pressure was 146 over 82.
The relative asked what would happen next.
The clinician explained that because the patient is on a blood thinner, a CT scan of the head is needed to check for internal bleeding, which would be done within a few hours.
The relative acknowledged the plan, saying, 'Okay.'
The clinician stated that the evening's dose of apixaban would be held until the scan was reviewed.
The patient agreed, saying, 'All right.'
The clinician stated that the nurse would clean the cut and close it with steri-strips and asked if the patient was up to date with tetanus.
The patient confirmed she was up to date with tetanus, stating, 'Yes, I had all of them.'
The clinician stated that if the scan is normal, the patient could go home with the daughter, who would stay with her for the next 24 hours.
The relative stated she would stay with the patient, saying, 'I'll stay with her.'
The clinician provided safety-netting advice: call 999 or return immediately if the patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
The relative acknowledged the safety-netting advice, saying, 'Okay, I will.'
